cards.stem: Which motion law keeps airspeed steady when net force is zero?
options: Newton’s First Law of Motion
Newton’s Second Law
Newton’s Third Law
Conservation of Energy Principle
cards.quote: Since there is no net external force on the aircraft, the aircraft maintains a constant airspeed as described by Newton’s First Law of Motion.
cards.hint: Think about what happens with balanced forces.

cards.stem: In steady level flight, which forces are described as balanced?
options: the lift is equal to the weight
the lift is equal to the drag
the weight is equal to the thrust
the drag is equal to the weight
cards.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.
cards.hint: Consider vertical and horizontal pairs separately.

cards.stem: What condition keeps ground speed steady during cruise?
options: as long as the wind speed is constant
as long as altitude stays constant
as long as fuel burn stays constant
as long as lift stays constant
cards.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.
cards.hint: Focus on wind influence on ground speed.

cards.stem: Maximum distance is ground speed multiplied by which time factor?
options: maximum time (tmax)
average cruise altitude
remaining fuel reserve
initial takeoff speed
cards.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).
cards.hint: Range depends on how long flight can last.
